stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy supplies a naloxone rescue kit to one walk-in requestor and has none readily available when a second walk-in asks for one an hour later. Which statements about what the pharmacy owes are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Counselling must be provided to the first requestor at the time of dispensing.
The opioid antagonist information pamphlet must be provided at that same time.
The second requestor must be referred to the nearest location holding stock.
The second requestor may simply be invited to return another day.
The referral duty applies even though this pharmacy cannot supply the product.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 9.06(3) requires counselling and the Board-approved opioid antagonist information pamphlet at the time of dispensing. 247 CMR 9.06(4) requires a pharmacy without one readily available at the time requested to refer the requestor to the nearest location that has one readily available. The referral duty exists precisely because the pharmacy cannot supply.

choice_analysis.A: Correct: counselling at the time of dispensing.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: the pamphlet accompanies the counselling.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: an affirmative referral to the nearest stocked location.
choice_analysis.D: An invitation to return does not discharge the referral duty.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: inability to supply is the trigger for the referral duty.

related_facts: The pamphlet is a Board-approved document
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates treat a stock-out as ending the pharmacy's obligations to the person in front of them.

reasoning_steps: Take the dispensing and the stock-out as two separate events
Apply the counselling and pamphlet duties to the dispensing
Apply the referral duty to the stock-out
